newsitem.title: ITALY: Washington's Cohen "encouraged" by Albania moves.
newsitem.headline: Washington's Cohen "encouraged" by Albania moves.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen on Friday welcomed Albanian President Sali Berisha's decision to suspend military action against insurgents.
Cohen, who was speaking in Rome, also said the United States had no specific plans to evacuate U.S. citizens from Albania, where armed rebels have seized control of a number of southern towns.

He said the unrest featured in his talks with Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini and Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta. Italy has urged Berisha and the Albanian opposition to form a broad-based government to resolve the crisis.

"Obviously the United States and Italy are prepared to work together to help resolve that situation," Cohen said. "This is primarily a political problem to be resolved and certainly not a military one but there has been a ceasefire and that is a very productive sign."

Cohen noted that a European Union mission by Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo was visiting Tirana on Friday to try to help secure a peaceful political settlement "so we are encouraged that there will be a positive result".
Berisha, backed by Albania's opposition parties, agreed on Thursday to suspend military activity against rebels for 48 hours and to offer an amnesty to those who surrendered weapons within two days.
Cohen said the United States always had contingency plans to evacuate U.S. nationals from countries where they might be in danger but no specific plans existed to pull some 1,600 out of Albania.
"We do not think the situation such that there have to be specific plans at this time but we remain prepared to act whenever it is essential to do so," he said.

Andreatta said Italy, which airlifted 35 foreigners from the southern Albanian port of Vlore on Monday, had also drawn up contingency plans for an evacuation but had no reports that Italians were in danger.
